tools.name: resolve_host
tools.description: Look up who hosts a URL and where an abuse/takedown notice would go. Identifies the CDN/proxy in front (e.g. Cloudflare), the platform, or the direct host and its abuse contact. For direct hosts and previously-revealed domains it returns the real host immediately; for a domain hidden behind a proxy

tools.name: assess_takedown
tools.description: Assess how a takedown for this URL would proceed: where the notice goes (host, platform, or a hidden host that must be revealed first), what documents and attestation the content owner must supply, the step-by-step process, and the legal caveats (§512(f), scope limits). Read-only; does not judge the

tools.name: start_takedown
tools.description: Get the secure onboarding link to actually start a takedown. The content owner opens it once in a browser to identify themselves, sign the standing authorization (the one step that legally requires a human), and provide proof of ownership. Returns the link plus what to prepare and what happens next.

tools.name: preserve_evidence
tools.description: Preserve a public web page as evidence BEFORE it disappears: a forensic-grade package — full-page screenshot, raw and rendered HTML, HTTP headers, hosting/registrar context, SHA-256 hashes of every artifact, an OpenTimestamps Bitcoin anchor and an Internet Archive snapshot — delivered to the USER'S

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "start_takedown" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Get the secure onboarding link to actually start a takedown. The content owner opens it once in a browser to identify themselves, sign the standing authorizatio…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "takedown" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: resolve_host, assess_takedown, start_takedown · Private data: resolve_host, assess_takedown · Public sink: preserve_evidence.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: resolve_host, assess_takedown, start_takedown · Private data: resolve_host, assess_takedown · Public sink: preserve_evidence

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
